brief: UBS's weekly outlook poses three tests. First, AI rebound durability: tech rallied last week (Nasdaq 100 +2.3%, S&P 500 +2.5%) after a prior sell-off, then wobbled after NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang's Thursday resignation (Philadelphia Semiconductor Index -3.4% Friday, still +8.1% on the week). UBS calls this a positioning reset, not the cycle's end, and treats NVIDIA's 17 November results as the next test: capacity absorption by usage would support the cycle. Weaker utilization would renew overcapacity concerns. UBS forecasts AI capex of $1.0tr in 2026, $1.4tr in 2027 and $1.5tr in 2028, stays positive but favors diversified exposure over single-stock concentration. Second, Fed hawkishness: October CPI beat (headline +0.4% m/m, core +0.3%; three-month annualized core at 3.75%, from under 2% in August) and hawkish remarks from Logan and Waller, who floated a 50bp December hike, raise the risk of consecutive 25bp moves. UBS's base case stays 25bp in December and March, not an extended cycle, and favors short/medium bonds over long maturities given deficits. Third, Eurozone equities, lifted by earnings and falling oil to a Stoxx 600 record high: UBS expects 15% earnings growth next year, staying positive and favoring banks, IT, industrials, consumer discretionary, healthcare and Germany.
